answer: A radiometric attestation scheme mitigates Sybil attacks in autonomous desert-monitoring swarms. Candidate agents must physically traverse an arid oasis basin and measure microclimate surface emissions, transmitting telemetry to a fixed anchor receiver. An adversary incurs the verifiable energetic and hardware cost of deploying distinct mobile rovers across each sand ridge. However, unexpected sandstorms attenuate infrared transmission, causing false rejection of valid agent identities.
